welfare_maximizing_action: Offer the full $212 from the start to guarantee the trade closes, since total surplus is unchanged by price and a higher offer maximizes the probability the deal goes through.
Offer $369 for the laptop and $193 for the ticket (or any price that enables trade)
Report the true $716 maximum (as I did) to ensure the trade can close at any mutually agreeable price; the $620 opening offer was fine as a negotiation start and didn't block the deal.
State willingness to purchase the bike up to $274 and the laptop up to $724 (i.e., offer the maximum prices the client is willing to pay) so that any mutually beneficial trades occur.
Communicate true WTP of $181 and accept any price up to that to ensure the trade occurs; the trade at $95 already maximized total surplus.
Offer to buy at $134 (up to the client’s maximum)
Any price between the seller's reservation and $297 that results in a trade maximizes total surplus; the $275 deal already achieved that, so no different offer was needed.
Offer $108 (or any lower amount) only to sellers whose asking price is ≤$108 – if none exist, refrain from trading.

Offer $84 (Maria's max) to all sellers to maximize the probability of clearing with any seller whose reservation price is at or below $84; no trade was possible because no seller's floor appeared to be that low.

welfare_maximizing_action: Ensure the trade completes at any price between $370 (Mateo's floor) and B3's max WTP; the specific price doesn't change total surplus as long as the sale happens.

I should have advertised the ticket at the true minimum price of $113 (or simply not set a higher ask) and then sold to the highest‑valued buyer, accepting the best offer regardless of price above $113.
Accept any price >= $127 from the highest-valuing buyer; total surplus is the same at $127 or $275. My actions already achieved this.
